semantic_contract: Non-virtual member of Editors::cEditorAnimWorld. ECX receiver, two callee-cleaned stack arguments (a creature id and an out pointer), byte-valued boolean return, no side effect of any kind on the receiver. It answers 'where is the animated creature registered under this creature id' and returns the answer as a 12-byte Math::Vector3. Invariants, in order: (1) if mpAnimWorld (+0x38) is null, return false without touching the map; (2) look the id up in mCreatures (+0x08) and return false if the lookup produced the map's end-of-tree sentinel, which is the receiver's own +0x0c; (3) because the key is now known to exist, the second map access is an operator[] whose insert branch is unreachable, so the map cannot grow as a side effect of a read; (4) load the controller's mpAnimatedCreature (+0x08) and return false if it is null; (5) otherwise copy three dwords from AnimatedCreature+0x04, which is AnimatedCreature::mPosition, into the caller's buffer as three separate dword stores and return true. None of the three failure paths writes the out buffer.
classification_rationale: The complete 104-byte body and both exits are read from the disassembly, the ABI is fixed by three independent register observations plus RET 0x8, every field offset the body touches is corroborated by the SDK's own layout declarations for three different classes, and the not-found test - the one instruction whose meaning is not self-evident - is resolved by reading the decompiled body of the find port rather than guessed. There is no virtual dispatch to leave unresolved and no global to read. The single withheld item is the original method name, which is a naming gap and not a behavioural one: the SDK declares five cEditorAnimWorld methods with address pairs and this address is none of them, so no identifier can be claimed without inventing one. The reconstructed behaviour itself carries no material uncertainty.
semantic_findings: This is the position-returning twin of the SDK-declared cEditorAnimWorld::GetAnimatedCreature: the two functions share a byte-identical three-step lookup preamble and differ only in what they do with the value slot.
The +0x38 gate is IAnimWorldPtr mpAnimWorld, so the whole query is refused when the animation world is not attached - the map may be populated but unreachable.

The middle guard is a pointer-identity test against the receiver's own +0x0c, which is the map's end-of-tree node. This is the standard EASTL 'find returned the sentinel' idiom and it is why a missing key is a false answer rather than an inserted default.

Because the find precedes the operator[], the map cannot be mutated by this read. The insertion path inside 0x0059c740 is dead code from this call site, which is a real invariant worth preserving in the reconstruction.

The payload is the animated creature's own mPosition, not the controller's mTargetPosition or mCurrentPosition: the controller pointer is dereferenced at +0x08 to reach the AnimatedCreature, and the copy starts four bytes into that object.

The three components are copied with three dword moves rather than one 12-byte move, and the third store is placed after the first POP, so the epilogue is interleaved with the payload write. A reconstruction that emitted a single 12-byte copy would be behaviourally equivalent but not structurally faithful.
Only AL is written on the success path, so bits 8..31 of EAX are undefined; every inspected caller tests the byte.

One caller at 0x00628f10 issues two back-to-back position queries with two different ids into two different buffers and never tests either return, relying on the buffers being pre-initialised. That is safe only because no failure path writes the buffer, which the body confirms.
This address is not in any vtable Ghidra has typed, consistent with a non-virtual query helper.
unresolved_questions: The original method name. cEditorAnimWorld declares five methods with address pairs and 0x0059d110 matches none of them, so the routine is either undeclared in the SDK or inlined out of a template. No name is claimed.

Why are only some of the 18 call sites checking the return value, and what do the unchecked ones do with a stale out buffer? The body guarantees the buffer is untouched on failure, but the callers' pre-initialisation was not verified.
Is the coordinate space of AnimatedCreature::mPosition world or model-local? The SDK does not say, and nothing in this body resolves it.
What are the 13 undisassembled call sites doing with the result, in particular the one at 0x0063a9ec that Ghidra does not attribute to any function?
Is there a sibling writer (a SetTargetPosition-shaped method at 0x59CF00) that this reader is the inverse of? Plausible from the signature but unverified here.
